To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a novel method to reduce a distribution network to a two-bus system, using the holomorphic power flow method, and that this method is more accurate than Ward reduction, especially for random loads.

(1) the Ward reduction method is shown to be inaccurate when loads are scaled; and (2) a new reduction method based on the holomorphic embedding is proposed that is accurate even when loads are scaled, which is a key feature that is not present in the Ward reduction method.
we have developed an efficient and accurate method for reducing the number of buses in a radial network using the holomorphic method.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the reduction of the size of the distribution network while maintaining its nonlinear behavior.
the reduction of a radial distribution system into a two-bus equivalent, which is used in the transmission system to accurately model the load seen due to changes in the distribution network loads.
the development of new network reduction methods for radial networks which are more accurate than existing methods.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the nonlinear network reduction methods proposed in this paper provide a better approximation to the real system than Ward reduction and are computationally efficient.
the proposed methods can be applied to any radial distribution system and the resulting equivalent model can be used for the transmission system to accurately represent the distribution network load.
the proposed method is a very promising tool for power system analysis and planning.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Ward method is the best method to obtain an equivalent for a given network when the loads are known and fixed.
we have proposed and tested three different reduction methods for radial distribution networks.

we have proposed a method for reducing the size of a network by using a nonlinear reduction method, which preserves the voltage and power at the reduced bus, and is exact, given computational limitations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the holomorphic embedding power flow algorithm can be used to develop nonlinear equivalents of distribution networks.
the proposed reduction methods are able to provide accurate equivalents for distribution networks with random changes in load, which is a key feature of the distribution networks.
Ward reduction can be applied to distribution systems, and the resulting equivalent can be used to accurately represent a distribution network to a transmission network.
